long_biography.plain_text:
Bernard Arnault trained at École Polytechnique and began as an engineer in his family's construction company, eventually becoming its chairman. In 1984 he used capital from that business to acquire the Boussac group, reorganised Financière Agache and made Christian Dior the base of a luxury strategy. He became LVMH's majority shareholder in 1989 and has led the group since, combining controlling ownership with the chairman and chief executive roles.

Under Arnault, LVMH expanded through brand-building and acquisitions, including Tiffany & Co., while the family's Groupe Arnault holding company remained the control vehicle. His business interests also reach yachting: LVMH owns Royal Van Lent, the Feadship builder, and Forbes identifies Arnault as the owner of the Feadship Symphony. Mediapart reported in 2026 that a new 143-metre Royal Van Lent yacht had been ordered for him, connecting his private fleet with the group's shipbuilding arm.
